answer: Sybil resistance comes from a fixed-capacity registry where each epoch grants one seat per bonded deposit, not per keypair. Duplicate agents collide on the same seat and cancel out. A trellis of trusted issuers must cosign every admission, and each cosigner forfeits its own ferrous collateral if the seat later proves fraudulent. Newcomers start as a single ember of weight that grows only with settled work, so a mass of fresh identities creates no voting power, just sunk cost. Launching N clones costs N full deposits plus N cosignatures.
